We started seeing a sharp increase in 500s and token-level latency around 07:45 PST this morning. Throughput dropped by ~40% on our real-time inference path and retries are causing downstream queueing.

Attached are a short summary and sample trace IDs. This is impacting appointment booking flows — we’ve pushed a rollback but need immediate triage and an ETA for remediation. Per our contract, this is a potential SLA breach; please escalate to engineering and sales leadership.

Thanks,
Julia

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:35 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Julia — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating to our SRE team now ...

We are seeing a cascading queuing effect in the request router tied to an edge autoscaling spike that led to partial KV cache thrashing for the gpt-small-cache model family used by Acme. Error rate peaked at 18% 500s; average 95p latency hit ~1.1s (baseline ~280ms). Initial mitigation: pin impacted traffic to a warmed pool and revert a recent router config pushed at 07:40 PST.

I will push the change now and monitor. I’ve attached raw request logs (redacted) and an incident trace to the Drive link. ETA for stabilization: 20–40 minutes if the warmed pool accepts traffic; if not, we may need a short maintenance window to rotate nodes.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Julia — quick update from our side: Marcus has applied the warmed-pool rollback and we’re seeing error rate trend down to ~2–3% and 95p latency improving. I’m opening an incident ticket and will publish a timeline + next steps in the shared Drive.

Separately, given the peak errors and the contractual SLA (99.9% availability / throughput targets in section 4.2), I’ll run a preliminary SLA impact calc and propose a remediation credit range. We’ll share that in the morning after we finish log reconciliation.

Monica Patel

Thanks for the quick fix — availability is improved but we saw two residual 10–15 minute regressions yesterday evening that bubbled up in our monitoring. We need a firm remediation plan and a clear credit calculation. Our procurement/legal team will expect a remediation credit that covers both the incident window and downstream operational costs (we logged a few hundred failed bookings that required manual reconciliation).

Please escalate to whoever owns commercial credits / exceptions — we’ll likely need an executive sign-off for amount > $40k.

Julia
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Julia Carter <julia.carter@acme-health.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health: throughput/latency incident — SLA remediation & credit discussion

Julia — thank you for the frank summary and for working with the team while we investigated. We completed the log reconciliation and validated the incident windows (2026-02-18 07:40–09:05 PST with two brief regressions on 02/18 20:10–20:25 and 02/19 19:40–19:55). Based on the contract (section 4.2) and the agreed calculation methodology, Redwood is prepared to offer a remediation credit equal to three days of committed capacity pricing (attached spreadsheet) and an additional one-time operational credit of $15,000 to help cover manual reconciliation costs.

We recognize the impact exceeded the target SLA and are committing to these steps:
- Formal post-incident report and RCA by next Wednesday (02/25).
- Free migration assistance to a warmed/high-availability routing profile for 30 days.
- Priority engineering on kernel selection improvements identified in the RCA.

If Acme needs a higher credit, we’re open to discussing escalation to Finance/Legal for an exception. Rishi / Monica will coordinate the acceptance and contract amendment.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
